samples.summary: Scope creep relative to the originating issue: a CI lane-graph restructure unrelated to font-preview subsetting. The issue (#963) is scoped to packages/frontend's font-catalog/pickers, declares "Architecture change? No", and lists no harness work; this delta splits `design-editor:build` out of `design-editor:check`, rewires three lanes' `needs`, and rewrites two design docs. docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-lessons.md:32 itself says the cause was "one commit earlier and elsewhere: #966" — i.e. a pre-existing main-branch breakage. It is defensible as the only way to make `pnpm verify:fast` green (an acceptance criterion), but it is a separable harness fix that would review better on its own, and it enlarges the blast radius of a frontend-only PR into the gating surface (harness.config.json + verify-self.mjs are both `ci.ciConfig` paths, forcing a full run and the ci-config-changed label).

Stale rationale now contradicted by this delta. The comment states "`@wafflebase/design-editor` is consumed as SOURCE. That package's `exports` map points at its `.ts` files" and that `allowImportingTsExtensions` "goes away when the package is published, because a build emits `.js` specifiers" — but since #966 `exports["."]` names `dist/plugin/index.js`, which is exactly what this delta rewrote the verify-self.mjs and harness-engineering.md comments to say. The flag may still be needed for the `./client` / `./scenes` / `./injector` subpaths, but the recorded reason is now wrong in the one package whose typecheck the new `needs: ["design-editor:build"]` edge exists for; a reader following the delta's reasoning lands here and is told the opposite.

Garbled paragraph, apparently an editing artifact: the new text ends "...is the shape to reach for whenever an inert package starts publishing a built entry: the general rule when listing a package inert: **enumerate every gate...**" — two colons splicing the new sentence into the pre-existing one, so neither reads as a complete sentence. The line break mid-phrase ("including\nknip") is the same artifact. This is the canonical harness doc; the rule it states is the one future authors will follow.

The exact regression this delta fixes has no lane-graph assertion. design-editor-packaging.md:152 now states a rule — "Anything that resolves `@wafflebase/design-editor` now needs a `needs: [\"design-editor:build\"]` edge" — but the lanes test still only asserts `design-editor:check`, `design-sandbox:check` and `verify:entropy` are selected for a designEditor-tagged change. Nothing asserts that a plain frontend-only change (the anyPkg → verify:entropy path, which is how this branch went red with `Could not parse knip output as JSON`) pulls `design-editor:build` into the closure, so deleting that edge would re-open the same failure silently.

The new lane runs the package's full `build` (`build:shell` + `build:plugin`), but the consumers the lane exists for — design-sandbox's typecheck and knip loading its vite.config.ts — only need `build:plugin`. Because `verify:entropy` now `needs` this lane on ANY package change, every PR in the repo pays the Vite shell build. The comment acknowledges the ride-along (~3s) and it also gives the shell build a CI home, so this is a taste call, not a defect; `build:plugin` for the shared edge plus `build:shell` inside `design-editor:check` would keep the cost where the risk is.

finding.summary: Recent rows for families outside the curated catalog carry no weight, so the preview falls back to wght@400 — the exact failure mode acceptance criteria 2 and 5 call out
finding.evidence: `data-font-weights={entry?.weights}` uses `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY` (the ~105-entry curated catalog). A family picked from the 1,908-entry full library is stored by `addRecentFont` as a bare string (font-recents.ts:53 stores names only) and is absent from the curated index, so `entry` is undefined, the attribute is absent, and `ensurePreviewFontLink` falls through to `previewWeight(undefined)` → `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS.split(';')[0]` → `400`. For a full-library family that ships no 400 cut (`Buda` 300, `UnifrakturCook` 700 — both named in the issue), css2 answers HTTP 400 and the row is stranded in a fallback face. Criterion 5 explicitly requires the weight be derived from what the row renders rather than a curated-catalog lookup that may miss.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: recents rows resolve weights only through `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY` (built from the curated `FONT_CATALOG`, font-family-picker.tsx:46-48), so `data-font-weights` is omitted for any family picked from the full library (font-family-picker.tsx:215-221). `font-recents.ts:33-66` persists bare family names only, so the information is unrecoverable after reload. The observer forwards the missing attribute (font-family-picker.tsx:120-127) and `ensurePreviewFontLink` falls through every guard because `CATALOG_INDEX` is curated-only (font-catalog.ts:91-93, 217-239), yielding `previewWeight(undefined)` → 400 (font-catalog.ts:184-187). The named examples are real and reachable: `font-catalog.full.ts:261` Buda = weights "300", `:1816` UnifrakturCook = "700", and neither is in `font-catalog.data.ts`; `applyPick` (font-family-picker.tsx:153-156) writes dialog picks from the full library into recents. This reproduces precisely the failure mode the issue's acceptance list forbids (docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md:35-38, 39-43; lessons.md:20-26 "Never assume weight 400 exists"), so it is a spec-conformance miss (major) in this lens, not a taste issue. The `findFontLink` no-op (font-catalog.ts:226) only helps within a session where a full link was already injected, so it is not a guard. The reviewer's criterion numbering is imprecise but the substance maps to a cited criterion, which is not a refutation ground.

finding.summary: Canonical design docs still describe the preview path as `ensureFontLink`; the loading-model change is recorded only in the source docstring and in docs/tasks, not folded into the subsystem design docs
finding.evidence: slides-fonts.md:177-184 and :201-202 ("Each visible row previews in its own family via an IntersectionObserver that calls `ensureFontLink` only for on-screen rows") and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:164 ("lazy-loads its CSS via `ensureFontLink(family, weights)` the first time a family is picked, hovered, or previewed") are now factually wrong: previewing goes through the new `ensurePreviewFontLink` with a new DOM contract (`data-wafflebase-font-preview`) and glyph subsetting. Neither doc, nor the `font-catalog.ts` row of the file table (docs-font-controls.md:76), was updated. Nested design docs are not link/ref-checked by CI, so nothing else catches this.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The source added a new preview loading path: font-catalog.ts:217 `ensurePreviewFontLink(family, text, weights?)` with its own DOM contract `data-wafflebase-font-preview` (font-catalog.ts:166-178, :201-204) and css2 `&text=` glyph subsetting; both preview observers now call it (more-fonts-dialog.tsx:151, font-family-picker.tsx:123). The canonical design docs were not updated: slides-fonts.md:177-184 still attributes "in-view preview in the dialog" to `ensureFontLink` and :201-202 still says the IntersectionObserver "calls `ensureFontLink` only for on-screen rows"; docs-font-controls.md:164 still says `ensureFontLink` runs when a family is "picked, hovered, or previewed", and its file table row for font-catalog.ts (:76) describes only "the `ensureFontLink` lazy loader". Both statements are now factually wrong. I searched wider than the reviewer: repo-wide grep for `ensurePreviewFontLink`/`data-wafflebase-font`/`text=`/`previewFont`, plus `glyph` and `subset|preview` across all 115 files under docs/design/** — the only records of the new model are docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-{todo,lessons}.md and source docstrings. No alternate canonical doc exists (no README in packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/). CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :57-61 require the existing subsystem design doc to be updated for a feature/non-trivial change, and the task plan contains no doc-update item. Under the design-fit rubric this is the named "design-doc discipline" violation (stale/unupdated canonical doc, change recorded only in a parallel task file) = major.
